title: Planner: tab support in Teams shared and private channels for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold pending a qualification to the organisation-wide Planner PowerShell control: unlike blocking the Teams app, it covers basic plans in Teams and Web, not premium plans on those surfaces. The roadmap details, enabled-by-default channel tab, channel membership rules and channel policy commands are supported.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block is the documented organisation-level app-blocking path.
claims.quote: In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is a documented organisation-level Planner disable command.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell. Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Blocking the Planner app in Manage apps blocks it across Teams for the organisation, rather than only in these channel types.
claims.quote: To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: The PowerShell switch turns off Planner for the organisation beyond Teams, with no plan-type qualification in the row.
claims.quote: This article applies to: Basic plans in the Planner app in Teams and Web; All plans in other Planner endpoints (including Planner mobile, and Planner connectors). For premium plans, see Disable Project for the web or Roadmap from Microsoft 365.
claims.fix: Replace the second sentence of controls[0].note and its rendered copy with: 'The PowerShell switch applies to basic plans in Teams and Web, and to all plans in other Planner endpoints, including Planner mobile and connectors; premium plans in Teams and Web require a different control.' The scope is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/disable-planner. Keep the existing plan-type qualification in the governance prose.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams > Teams policies > policy > Edit > Create private channels controls private-channel creation.
claims.quote: go to Teams > Teams policies. Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then click Edit. Create private channels: When On, team owners and members can create private channels.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsChannelsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowPrivateChannelCreation $false prohibits private-channel creation under that policy.
claims.quote: -Identity: Use this parameter to specify the name of the policy being updated. -AllowPrivateChannelCreation: Determines whether a user is allowed to create a private channel. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this FALSE to prohibit.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams > Teams policies > policy > Edit > Create shared channels controls whether team owners can create shared channels.
claims.quote: go to Teams > Teams policies. Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then click Edit. Create shared channels: When On, team owners can create shared channels.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsChannelsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowSharedChannelCreation $false disables shared-channel creation under that policy.
claims.quote: [-AllowSharedChannelCreation <Boolean>] -AllowSharedChannelCreation: Team owners can create shared channels for people within and outside the organization. -Identity: Use this parameter to specify the name of the policy being updated.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams > Teams policies > policy > Edit > Invite external users to shared channels controls invitations from trusted external organisations.
claims.quote: go to Teams > Teams policies. Select the policy ... then click Edit. Invite external users to shared channels: When On, owners and members of shared channels can invite external participants from organizations where a cross-organization trust has been configured.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsChannelsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelSharingToExternalUser $false controls shared-channel owners' external invitations.
claims.quote: [-AllowChannelSharingToExternalUser <Boolean>] Owners of a shared channel can invite external users to join the channel if Microsoft Entra external sharing policies are configured.

claims.claim: External members or teams already added retain channel access when AllowChannelSharingToExternalUser is set to FALSE.
claims.quote: If the channel has been shared with an external member or team, they will continue to have access to the channel even if this parameter is set to FALSE.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowTeamsChannelContainerAccess $false disables Planner tabs in shared and private channels tenant-wide.
claims.quote: run the following command to disable the Planner tab for shared and private channels in your tenant. Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowTeamsChannelContainerAccess $false

claims.claim: Disabling the channel-tab experience blocks access to existing plans created from shared and private channels.
claims.quote: Disabling this experience blocks access to: Any existing plans created from shared and private channels

claims.claim: Disabling the channel-tab experience prevents creation of new plans in those channel types.
claims.quote: Disabling this experience blocks access to: Creation of new plans from shared and private channels

claims.claim: Setting AllowTeamsChannelContainerAccess to $true re-enables the channel-tab experience.
claims.quote: If you change your mind and want to enable the Planner tab for shared and private channels in your tenant, run the following command: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowTeamsChannelContainerAccess $true

claims.claim: The organisation-wide Planner disable page is addressed to global admins.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Planner admin page points to a custom app permission policy for allowing or blocking Planner for specific users.
claims.quote: make sure Planner is turned on for your organization on the Manage apps page, and then create a custom policy for app permissions and assign it to those users.

claims.claim: Teams policy changes may take 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: After you edit the global policy or assign a policy, it may take 24 hours for changes to take effect.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide Planner disable article applies to basic plans in Teams and Web.
claims.quote: This article applies to: Basic plans in the Planner app in Teams and Web

claims.claim: The organisation-wide Planner disable article applies to all plans in other Planner endpoints.
claims.quote: All plans in other Planner endpoints (including Planner mobile, and Planner connectors).

claims.claim: The Create shared channels setting makes organisation-available Teams apps available in shared channels.
claims.quote: Create shared channels: When On, team owners can create shared channels. Teams apps that are available for your organization are also available in shared channels.
